solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The French speaker taken in by test centre

parts.note: la is the French feminine form of 'the'

indicators.note: being taken in by something puts this word inside the next one

parts.note: taken as written
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A French-speaking person is taken in for questioning at a testing centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'by' looks like a mere link, yet it is the container that the speaker sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a place where tests and experiments are carried out.

clue.text: Lap at speed

definitions.meaning: to lap is to take up with the tongue, as a cat does
a ... is a fast pace, as in 'at a great ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a tongue stroke and an informal word for a rapid pace.

clue.text: Gun man runs in

indicators.note: in places the runs letter within the man's name

parts.note: Ben is a man's name
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A gunman comes running in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun man' reads as gunman, but 'Gun' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bren was a British light machine weapon used in the Second World War.

clue.text: The financier's new clothes?

parts.note: a fresh 'vestment' put on again reads as ..., putting money back in, which a financier does

explanation.surface: A play on the emperor's new clothes, applied to a money man.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-IN-VESTMENT, it means dressing again in new garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughing profits back into a venture is the financier's stock activity.

clue.text: Holding cross over river

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'over' puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a cross, X, is the Roman numeral for ten
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone holds on while crossing over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding of land or an office, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Back in good health, add new parts

parts.note: retro means backwards or harking back
fit means healthy

explanation.surface: Someone back in good health is having replacement parts fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrofit is to install components a machine lacked when first built.

clue.text: Some of the goods offered make one curse

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some items on sale are so poor they make a shopper swear.
explanation.definitionFit: Odso is an old oath or exclamation, the sort of thing a vexed person utters.

clue.text: Lookout killing first crawler

indicators.note: first puts the killing word before the lookout word

parts.note: a killing is a death
a watch is a lookout

explanation.surface: A sentry is the first to be killed.
explanation.walkthrough: The deathwatch beetle bores through old timber and is known for its ticking.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling the beetle a crawler is a loose but fair description of an insect.

clue.text: Where those captive are free?

parts.note: a paradox: a jail with minimal security where inmates have relative liberty

explanation.surface: A riddle about a place where prisoners are at liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimum-security jail lets inmates move about and even work outside.

clue.text: Tick line on voucher

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, buying now and paying later
a line is a short letter, as in 'drop me a line', i.e. a note

explanation.surface: Someone ticks a line on a voucher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' looks like a checkmark but here means credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit note is a slip a shop gives instead of a refund, to spend later.

clue.text: You and I accepted £1,000 during vigil

indicators.note: accepted means the pair took the thousand inside

parts.note: you and I together are we
a thousand pounds is a K, a grand, read here as 'a K'

explanation.surface: A couple take a thousand pounds during a funeral vigil.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay needs 'a' before the K; the clue omits it, so £1,000 must be read as 'a thousand', A plus K.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake is a watch kept over the body of the dead before burial.

clue.text: Income charge

parts.note: read as 'in-come charge': the price paid for coming in

explanation.surface: Sounds like a levy on earnings, such as income tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The price of entry to a venue is paid on coming in, hence the split reading.

clue.text: Position of feudal superior on master vessel

parts.note: on can mean over, upon
a lord is a master
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A medieval lord's rank, put on a master vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlord was the superior in the feudal chain, and the suffix gives his rank or office.

clue.text: Agent for cleric stopping short having no right

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: stopping short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a curate is a junior clergyman
O looks like zero, nothing, no

explanation.surface: An agent acting for a clergyman who stops short and has no right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping short' trims the last letter of CURATE to give CURAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurator is one who manages affairs on another's behalf, a legal representative.

clue.text: Crybaby suffered random pain

indicators.note: suffered suggests the letters were put through a painful upheaval and reworked

explanation.surface: A crybaby makes a fuss over some random pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is a temperamental, self-important person who throws tantrums.

clue.text: Most unusual to find a rector amongst all the others

indicators.note: amongst puts the pair inside the word for the others

parts.note: the rest means all the others

explanation.surface: It is very rare to find a rector among everybody else.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go after the first letter of REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Most unusual is the superlative of rare, both meaning seldom found.

clue.text: Leading tribesman entered Bairiki travelling round country

indicators.note: entered puts the leading letter inside the rearranged place name
travelling round says the place name's letters are moved about
leading means the front letter of the tribesman

explanation.surface: A tribal leader goes into Bairiki on a tour of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Bairiki is the capital islet of the country; 'travelling round' rearranges it to KIRIBAI, and the T goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiribati is a Pacific island nation, so it is simply an example of a country.

clue.text: Sort provided's elegant on the outside

indicators.note: the elegant word is on the outside, wrapped round the condition word

parts.note: classy means elegant
provided is means if

explanation.surface: Something sorted is elegant, at least on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort is to arrange items into categories or groups.

clue.text: Roughly order in distance medicinal plant

parts.note: ca, circa, means roughly

indicators.note: in places the order inside the distance

parts.note: a mile is a distance
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A rough order for a medicinal plant, from a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Camomile is a herb whose flowers are used in soothing teas and remedies.

clue.text: Unbalanced new spy chief had nothing on

indicators.note: new says the letters are made anew in another order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An unstable new spymaster had nothing on.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbalanced here is an adjective for mentally unstable, a colloquial psychotic sense.

clue.text: Daughter in the country becoming gentle youth

indicators.note: in places the daughter letter within the country

parts.note: Chile is a South American country

explanation.surface: A daughter living abroad turns into a gentle youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gentle' is the old sense of well-born, as in gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A childe was a young man of noble birth, as in Byron's Childe Harold.

clue.text: After lessons its pupils should stay on

definitions.text: After lessons its pupils should stay on

parts.words: After lessons its pupils should stay on
parts.note: staying on reads as staying after school, but means staying in the saddle

explanation.surface: Pupils kept behind after lessons, as at detention.
explanation.definitionFit: Students learning horsemanship must keep their seat on the mount once taught.

clue.text: Graduate with nothing less than hot money

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: less than means the nothing letter is taken away

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A graduate has nothing but a bit of hot money.
explanation.definitionFit: The baht is the currency unit of Thailand.

clue.text: Equipment changed for hill-climbing

definitions.meaning: a driver shifts to a lower one of these to climb a hill

explanation.definitionFit: Gear means kit, and a car's gear is what is changed on a slope.

clue.text: Seaweed that's brown and green to start with

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: to start with means the first letter of green

explanation.surface: Seaweed that is brown with a touch of green at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tang is a coarse brown seaweed, a kind of wrack.

clue.text: Restaurant-car menu?

parts.note: on a train the dining list sits beside the fare paid for the ticket

explanation.surface: A railway dining car's list of dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: On a train, 'fare' is both the food and the ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old-fashioned phrase for a menu, a list of dishes offered.

clue.text: Walk having no time for study

indicators.note: having no means the time letter is removed

parts.note: to tread is to walk

explanation.surface: Someone out walking has no time to study.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject at university is to study it, a British usage.

clue.text: Peter testy about printer

indicators.note: about says the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Peter is irritable about a printer.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter arranges type for printing, so the job is part of a printer's trade.
